question: GQ-004
subject: how far the numFound-overstates-works finding actually generalises
the_claim_i_made: "IA's reported pool size is not the number of distinct works, so every earlier figure in this thread using numFound as a work count was inflated."
correction: WRONG AS STATED. Five of six pools have ZERO duplicate titles. Only science fiction has any, at 13.6%. "Every earlier figure was inflated" generalised from one pool to all of them — the same error I made with the 97.5% overlap two loops ago, and again with the "pessimistic bias" one loop ago.

what_the_duplicates_actually_are.reading: Same work scanned multiple times, not a pagination artifact. Specific to a heavily re-scanned pulp-magazine corpus.

the_honest_version: numFound can overstate distinct works where a pool contains repeated scans of the same item. Measured here: 13.6% in science fiction, 0% in five other subjects. It is a property of particular collections, not of IA search.
third_time: This is the third loop running where I generalised from a single measurement: overlap from science fiction, sampling bias from four subjects, duplication from one pool. In each case the next measurement contradicted it. The pattern is not that I measure badly — it is that I state the conclusion at the scope I wish I had measured rather than the scope I did.
